name: Brow lift / brow bone augmentation

lead: A brow lift raises a low or drooping eyebrow and can smooth forehead lines. Techniques range from botulinum toxin and fillers to endoscopic, temporal and direct surgical lifts. In looksmaxxing communities it is often listed alongside other hardmaxxing procedures, because brow position and brow ridge projection are discussed as part of the eye area.

Brow bone augmentation or reduction reshapes the bony ridge above the eyes using implants, grafts, cement or burring. The published literature on this sits mostly within craniofacial and gender-affirming surgery rather than appearance enhancement in general, and no trials were found testing it for looksmaxxing goals.

paras: Surgical lifts release and reposition the forehead and brow soft tissue, often by altering the depressor muscles and fixing the brow higher; endoscopic approaches use small scalp incisions. Botulinum toxin can raise the brow by weakening the muscles that pull it down. Bone augmentation adds material over the supraorbital ridge or frontal bone, while reduction removes or recontours bone.

Reviews describe complications of brow lifts including scalp numbness, hair loss at incisions, hairline change, asymmetry, infection and bleeding, with technique-specific differences, and note that no brow lift technique is considered completely satisfactory in longevity. Non-surgical options are temporary. Forum participants discuss surgery abroad and the risk of poor results.

lead: A brow lift (also forehead lift, browplasty or browpexy) is a cosmetic or reconstructive procedure that raises a low or drooping eyebrow and may soften forehead lines [1][2]. Techniques include endoscopic, coronal, direct, temporal, hairline and transblepharoplasty approaches, plus non-surgical options such as botulinum toxin and soft tissue fillers [1][2]. A published review of ten popular techniques concluded that none is completely satisfactory because of limited effectiveness, longevity or complications [1].

In looksmaxxing and hardmaxxing discussion, brow lifts are listed within multi-procedure plans, for example alongside genioplasty, lip lift, canthoplasty and blepharoplasty, often performed abroad [3][4]. Community posts also discuss brow bone implants and reducing frontal bossing, a separate group of procedures involving the skeleton rather than soft tissue. Published work on brow bone contouring is concentrated in facial feminization and masculinization surgery, where forehead reduction or augmentation is an established part of gender-affirming care.

Evidence for soft-tissue brow lifting consists mainly of surgical case series, narrative reviews and a limited number of small randomized trials; no trial has tested brow bone augmentation for appearance enhancement in people without gender-affirming or reconstructive indications.

paras: Brow lifting addresses eyebrow descent (brow ptosis) that can occur with aging, and may also be used to change brow shape or position in younger people. Reviews describe the upper third of the face as an area where both bone and soft tissue contribute to appearance. The procedure can be done alone or with upper eyelid surgery, and some reviews note that total brow ptosis calls for a forehead lift while lateral ptosis can be handled with a temporal approach [5].

The Wikipedia article on the procedure lists endoscopic lifts (a camera and instruments through a few small scalp incisions), coronal lifts (a long scalp incision), direct, mid-forehead, pretrichial, temporal and internal approaches, and notes that botulinum toxin is sometimes used alongside surgery [6].

A review of the endoscopic brow lift describes correcting brow ptosis by altering depressor muscles in combination with wide subperiosteal undermining, and describes technical pitfalls that lead to less-than-ideal outcomes [2]. Another review calls the endoscopic brow lift an established procedure that can safely and reliably rejuvenate the upper third of the face [7]. A surgeon's personal series of 538 patients compared fixation techniques for endoscopic lifts [8].

A subcutaneous lateral temporal lift has been described as a more recent technique that elevates the lateral brow with minimal complications, according to its senior author [9]. The direct brow lift, in which an incision is made just above the brow, has been evaluated for efficacy, complications and patient satisfaction [10].

Neuromodulators can elevate the brows and improve periorbital lines, and fillers can camouflage some periorbital contour changes, according to a 2024 review [11]. Reviews state that non-surgical forehead and brow lifts are temporary and require less experience, and that correction is easier if a complication occurs [1]. A controlled study found brow elevation after botulinum toxin is theorized to result from inactivating brow depressors [12], and an earlier case series reported brow elevation after toxin injection directed to the brow area [13]. A split-face trial reported that injecting toxin at different depths was not effective for correcting brow asymmetry [12]. Energy-based skin tightening devices have also been studied for brow lifting in small trials and cohort studies [14][15].

The brow ridge and frontal bone can be augmented or reduced. In facial feminization, forehead contouring may involve reduction of the brow and frontal bone, orbital contouring and hairline adjustment, and a 2023 review reports that these procedures are well tolerated with minimal side effects reported despite the proximity to the frontal sinus and cranial vault. In facial masculinization, forehead augmentation can use custom implants, planned from CT scans. These are mainly gender-affirming procedures, and the evidence base consists of reviews and case series.

Reviews describe brow lifting as able to raise the brow and improve upper face appearance, with long-term before-and-after photographs offered as evidence of efficacy for the endoscopic technique [2]. A comparative study of 538 endoscopic patients examined fixation methods, and a randomized comparison in women having upper blepharoplasty looked at temporal brow lift versus internal browpexy for lateral brow elevation [8][16]. A review of aging eyebrow shape found that eyebrow position and shape change with age, informing surgical goals [17], and a 1996 study related brow lift outcomes to aesthetic ideals for eyebrow height and shape in women [18].
A 2020 narrative review of 56 selected references concluded that none of the techniques is completely satisfactory because of limited effectiveness, lack of longevity and potential complications [1].

Wikipedia reports that about 1% of endoscopic procedures are converted to open surgery, that hairline lifts had the highest revision rates, numbness was most common with direct lifts and hair loss with endoscopic lifts, and that coronal lifts carry a higher risk of raising the frontal hairline and reducing scalp sensation [6]. Infection and bleeding are possible with any surgery [6]. A review of endoscopic browplasty discusses potential complications and means to reduce them [7].

Scarring is relevant for direct brow lifts, and trials have examined laser treatment of direct browplasty scars [19]. Botulinum toxin carries its own temporary side effect risks, such as unintended brow position changes.

Members of looksmax.org describe brow lifts as one component of multi-procedure surgery plans, sometimes in the same trip as genioplasty, lip lift, cheek implants and eyelid surgery, with one poster reporting a total cost of about 15,000 US dollars for a package performed in Turkey [3][20]. Other threads are titled around lateral brow lift feedback, brow bone implants and botulinum toxin to lower the brow position [21][22][23]. Posters also ask how to find surgeons to avoid poor results [3].

Human studies of brow lifting exist but are mostly case series and small trials. Examples include a randomized comparison of temporal brow lift versus internal browpexy in women having upper blepharoplasty [16], a randomized trial of botulinum toxin on eyebrow height after glabellar injection [24], a split-face trial of botulinum toxin injection depth for brow asymmetry [12], a randomized study of ultrasound rejuvenation for upper facial skin [25], and a rater-blinded cohort of ultrasound tightening for brow lift [14]. A controlled trial of a laser for direct browplasty scars enrolled nine patients [19]. Registered trials include botulinum toxin for brow ptosis (Dysport, 24 participants) and devices for non-surgical brow lifting [26][27].
No studies were found of brow bone augmentation performed for looksmaxxing purposes; related evidence comes from facial feminization and masculinization reviews.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, brow lifts and brow bone work are discussed as part of hardmaxxing plans and surgery trips, with threads on lateral lifts, brow implants and botulinum toxin [3][21][22][23].

claims.claim: A brow lift can fix a low or tired-looking brow position as part of a wider facial overhaul.
Brow bone implants or augmentation can create a stronger, more masculine brow ridge.
Botulinum toxin can raise or reshape the brow without surgery.
Surgery abroad, such as in Turkey, is a cost-effective route for brow and facial procedures.

timeline.event: German surgeon Erich Lexer writes the first documented medical discussion of forehead lifting [6].
The coronal technique is widely used before declining in favor of endoscopic methods [6].
Facial feminization surgery, including forehead work, begins to develop through Douglas Ousterhout and colleagues [28].
A prospective case series reports temporal brow elevation after botulinum toxin A [13].
A 538-patient personal series on endoscopic brow lift is published [8].
